editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world where almost everyone is gone. You are stuck in a dusty airplane hangar in Colorado with nothing but your dog and a grumpy guy with a gun for company. That is exactly where you start in this story. The vibe is very lonely and quiet at first, but it feels real. You really get a sense of how boring and scary life is when you are one of the last people left on Earth. Everything changes when a strange voice comes through the radio while the main character is flying his old plane, and suddenly, the movie turns into a giant treasure hunt to find where that signal is coming from.

Ridley Scott does a great job making the empty landscapes look beautiful and scary at the same time. The acting is solid, especially the bond between the man and his dog, which will definitely pull at your heartstrings. While the middle part slows down a bit, the ending makes up for it with some big surprises.
endingExplained: At the very end, you find out the radio signal was not from another survivor, but an automated loop from an old government base. However, while searching the base, the main character finds a hidden bunker with a small group of people who actually survived the plague. The twist is that the gunman was secretly working for them all along. It ends on a hopeful note as they start building a new town together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about the end of the world and loyal dogs.
